How ad credit works

Sign up, then run an eligible campaign

Signing up or adding a payment method is not enough. If your account shows a spend-and-get-credit offer, you must spend the eligible amount on ads within the stated period. Credit may then be added for future ads under the offer terms; it is not cash back.

Example: if your account offers “spend $200, get $200” and you spend $200 in eligible ads within the deadline, you may receive $200 in ad credit for a later campaign. You pay for the first $200 yourself.

FAQs

Answers before you start

Is TikTok Ads right for my business?

It is worth testing if you have a clear offer, an audience, and a way to measure visits, inquiries, or orders.

Do I need an online store?

No. Depending on available objectives, you can promote a website, service, or app. Prepare a clear landing page or contact path.

What budget should I start with?

Choose a test budget you can afford. Check the minimums in Ads Manager and compare the cost per result with your margins.

Does TikTok guarantee sales?

No. Results depend on the product, offer, video, landing page, audience, and measurement. Treat your first campaign as a test.

Who may qualify for the new advertiser offer?

Eligibility depends on your new ad account, account country, advertising history, and the offer shown by TikTok. Review the terms in Ads Manager.

Is the $6,000 credit guaranteed or withdrawable?

No. Some offers may have a maximum of $6,000, but TikTok determines eligibility, amount, country, and spending requirements. Ad credit is for advertising, not cash withdrawal.
